clue.text: Unite share round what gets party going

indicators.note: to go round something is to enclose it, so one piece wraps the other
what starts a word going is its opening letter, so only the beginning is kept

blocks.note: a slice is a share or portion
the first letter of party

explanation.surface: Someone wants to bring a group together by sharing round whatever gets a party going.
explanation.definitionFit: To splice is to join two ends, as of ropes or film, so it is a synonym of unite.

clue.text: Render unintelligible — to wit, rabbit on

blocks.note: SC abbreviates scilicet, Latin for 'to wit' or 'namely'
to rabbit on is British slang for talking at length, i.e. to ramble

explanation.surface: A wry remark that rambling talk makes a speaker incomprehensible.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'rabbit on' is British slang for chattering on and on.
explanation.definitionFit: To scramble a signal or message is to jumble it so that it cannot be understood.

clue.text: Support is nothing in Roman law as a whole

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another means it is placed inside it

blocks.note: a leg supports a table or chair
taken as written
Latin was the language of the Romans
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A legal pronouncement that the backing of Roman law counts for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Legislation is the body of laws enacted, i.e. law taken collectively.

clue.text: Junior team player left in bed

indicators.note: one thing lying in another means it is placed inside it

blocks.note: a cot is a small bed
L is the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A youth-team player has been left behind, still in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: In sport, a colt is a young or inexperienced player, especially in a junior cricket side.

clue.text: Set off lad about hag

indicators.note: to be about something is to surround it, so one piece goes round the other

blocks.note: a son is a lad
a hag is an ugly old witch

explanation.surface: A boy flees, startled by an old crone.
explanation.definitionFit: To set off a machine or alarm is to activate it, which is to turn it on.

clue.text: Web isn't a free place to put junk

indicators.note: letters set free are loosed from their order and can be rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of these words, apostrophe dropped
taken as written, part of the fodder

explanation.surface: A grumble that the internet is not a free-for-all dumping ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'a' before 'free' looks like a mere article but its letter joins the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A wastebin is a receptacle for rubbish, the obvious spot for discarding junk.

clue.text: Luvvie's wild recital that must be cut short

indicators.note: something wild is unruly and disordered, so the letters are thrown out of order
cutting a word short trims off its final letter

blocks.note: taken as written
the word with its last letter cut

explanation.surface: A luvvie's over-the-top recital is so wild it needs trimming.
explanation.walkthrough: A luvvie is British slang for a gushing, self-regarding actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything belonging to a luvvie, an affected actor, is stagey, so the possessive stands for the adjective.

clue.text: Actor who overdoes it let off from the bard's play

indicators.note: the phrase splits: the word let is taken off from what follows

blocks.note: taken as written; this is what is removed
Hamlet is Shakespeare's play; the Bard is Shakespeare

explanation.surface: A hammy actor is excused from appearing in the Shakespeare production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let off' reads as pardoned, but it means remove the word let.
explanation.definitionFit: A ham is a performer who overacts, exaggerating every gesture and line.

clue.text: Annoyed by chest in study being overturned

indicators.note: something overturned is upended, so in a down clue the word reads backwards
one thing sitting in another means it is placed inside it

blocks.note: a den is a private study
an ark is a chest or box, as in the Ark of the Covenant

explanation.surface: Someone is irritated by a chest in their study being knocked over.
explanation.walkthrough: Narked is British slang for irritated.
explanation.definitionFit: Narked is informal British slang meaning irritated or put out.

clue.text: Get slices of egg and lettuce for this roll

indicators.note: a slice is a thin piece cut from the front, so only the leading letter of each word is kept

blocks.note: to bag something is to get it
first letters of egg and lettuce

explanation.surface: A sandwich order: egg and lettuce slices to fill the roll.
explanation.definitionFit: A bagel is a ring-shaped bread roll, boiled then baked.

clue.text: Algeria's lost trappings of ceremony?

indicators.note: a country that is lost has gone astray, so its letters wander out of order

blocks.note: the country name, taken as letters

explanation.surface: Algeria has mislaid the pomp of its state occasions.
explanation.definitionFit: Regalia are the emblems and robes of rank worn or carried at formal ceremonies.

clue.text: What healthy chef uses an old packet?

blocks.note: first meaning: a pan for cooking food over vapour, a healthy method
second meaning: a steam-driven ship, once called a packet boat

explanation.walkthrough: A packet was a ship carrying mail on a regular route; 'packet' suggests a parcel.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a vapour-cooking pan and a steamship, such as an old mail packet.

clue.text: Millions question cover

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for million
to ask is to question

explanation.surface: Millions are asking questions about a cover-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A mask is something that covers the face, so it is a kind of covering or disguise.

clue.text: Delightful Democrat is likely candidate

blocks.note: D abbreviates Democrat
a candidate likely to win is electable

explanation.surface: A charming Democrat looks a probable winner.
explanation.definitionFit: Delectable means delicious or highly pleasing, a close synonym.

clue.text: Set at ease tame techie that struggles

indicators.note: something that struggles twists and writhes, so its letters are contorted into a new order

blocks.note: to break a horse is to tame it
the letters of this word, rearranged

explanation.surface: Putting a nervous techie at ease by taming his struggles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tame techie' looks like the anagram fodder, but tame is a separate verb piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To break the ice is to dispel awkwardness at a first meeting, relaxing people.

clue.text: Final edit in five changes

indicators.note: changes alters the arrangement, so the letters are shuffled into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of these words

explanation.surface: The final edit has been done in five rounds of changes.
explanation.definitionFit: A definitive version is the conclusive one, settling matters, as a final text does.

clue.text: Depressing retreat behind pasture

indicators.note: one piece coming behind another is placed after it in the reading order

blocks.note: a lea is a meadow or pasture
a den is a private retreat

explanation.surface: A gloomy hideaway stands behind a meadow.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaden means heavy and dull in mood, so it describes something depressing.

clue.text: Kicked off about short film being split

indicators.note: to be about something is to surround it, so one piece goes round the other

blocks.note: kicked off is slang for died
vid is a clipped form of video

explanation.surface: A short film started up and opinion was divided.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kicked off' looks like started, but here it is slang for dying.
explanation.definitionFit: Divided is the past participle of divide, meaning separated into parts, the same as split.

clue.text: Items doc ordered for char

indicators.note: things ordered are put into a new sequence, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of these words

explanation.surface: A doctor's shopping list sent off for a cleaner to fetch.
explanation.walkthrough: A char, short for charwoman, is a British term for a cleaning lady.
explanation.definitionFit: A domestic is a household servant, and a char is a cleaner employed in the home.

clue.text: Scoundrels after time trained horses

indicators.note: one piece coming after another is placed behind it in the reading order

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
rotters are scoundrels

explanation.surface: Rogues have been at work after hours on racehorses.
explanation.definitionFit: Trotters are horses trained to race at a trot, as in harness racing.

clue.text: It fills Peak traveller?

indicators.note: a thing that fills another goes inside it

blocks.note: the peak of a cap is its visor
taken as written

explanation.surface: A question about a tourist crowding the Peak District.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital P makes Peak look like the Peak District, but it means the brim of a cap.
explanation.definitionFit: A visitor is someone who travels to a place, as a traveller does.

clue.text: Comparatively gross officer who was once a squaddie?

definitions.text: officer who was once a squaddie?

blocks.note: first meaning: more rank, i.e. more foul

blocks.clueFragment: officer who was once a squaddie?
blocks.note: second meaning: an officer risen from the ranks

explanation.walkthrough: A squaddie is British slang for a private soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Ranker is the comparative of rank (foul) and also a term for a commissioned officer promoted from the ranks.

clue.text: High-flying son first to insure… vehicle with you and me

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter, which alone is kept

blocks.note: first letter of insure
a car is a vehicle
us means you and me

explanation.surface: A high-flying son must insure the family car first.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Icarus, son of Daedalus, flew too near the sun on wax wings.
explanation.definitionFit: Icarus was the mythical son who flew so high that the sun melted his wings.

clue.text: With no positive delight for contract

indicators.note: with no means without, so that letter is taken away

blocks.note: P abbreviates positive
to please is to delight

explanation.surface: Sombrely signing a contract, with no positive pleasure in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A lease is a legal agreement letting property for a term, a kind of contract.

clue.text: Against getting into smart support from one side

indicators.note: something getting into another goes inside it

blocks.note: clever means smart
anti means against

explanation.surface: Someone opposed to a smart idea is getting support from one side.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantilever is a beam fixed at only one end, bearing load from that one side.

clue.text: Involved with the smallest thing

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters are mixed into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of this word

explanation.surface: Getting involved with the tiniest detail.
explanation.definitionFit: A whit is the least possible amount, as in 'not a whit', i.e. a tiny bit.

clue.text: Murder victim's description lacking first line

indicators.note: lacking means without, and first pins the removal to the opening letter

blocks.note: a label is a descriptive tag
L abbreviates line

explanation.surface: A police description of a murder victim missing its opening line.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'victim's' reads as 'is': Abel is the murder victim; Abel was killed by his brother Cain in Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible Abel was slain by Cain, the first murder victim.

clue.text: What you give for bread? Husband ignored the price oddly

indicators.note: something ignored is left out, so that letter is dropped
oddly means in a strange way, so the letters are set out in a strange order

blocks.note: H abbreviates husband
the letters of these words

explanation.surface: A shopper's husband ignored the odd price on a loaf.
explanation.walkthrough: Bread is slang for money, not the loaf; take H out of 'the price' before rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: A receipt is the written acknowledgement handed over when money, slang bread, is received.

clue.text: Endless staff for prison

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is chopped off

blocks.note: a cane is a walking staff

explanation.surface: Prison staff working endless shifts.
explanation.definitionFit: The can is American slang for jail, a synonym of prison.

clue.text: It's majestic being under a tree

blocks.note: sub means under
a lime is a tree, the linden

explanation.surface: Lying in the shade of a tree is a wonderful feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Sublime means awe-inspiringly grand or exalted, close to majestic.

clue.text: Judge's dispatched, thus start of hearing is cancelled

indicators.note: the opening letter of hearing is cancelled, meaning that letter is struck out

blocks.note: sent means dispatched
hence means thus, therefore

explanation.surface: The judge has sent someone down, so the start of the hearing is called off.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove H, the start of hearing, from HENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge pronounces a sentence, so the punishment handed down is the judge's.

clue.text: Nippers in peril running about close to cars

indicators.note: running about is moving here and there, so the letters scatter into a new order
the close of a word is its end, so only its last letter is kept

blocks.note: the letters of this word
last letter of cars

explanation.surface: Children are in danger running about near cars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nippers' suggests children, but it means gripping tools.
explanation.definitionFit: Pliers are pincer-like hand tools, and nippers is another name for such gripping tools.
